headline: You can already vote in Virginia. Early voting started Sept. 18.

deadlines.label: Early in-person voting starts
deadlines.detail: At your local voter registration office or a satellite location.

deadlines.label: Sunday early voting
deadlines.detail: Local voter registration offices open for in-person voting.

deadlines.label: Last day to register (regular ballot)
deadlines.detail: Also the last day to update your address. After this you can still register in person through Election Day, but you'll vote a provisional ballot.

Saturday early voting
deadlines.detail: Local voter registration offices open for in-person voting.

deadlines.label: Sunday early voting
deadlines.detail: Local voter registration offices open for in-person voting.

deadlines.label: Last day of early voting
deadlines.detail: In person at your local voter registration office. Official page: through 5:00 p.m.

deadlines.label: Election Day
deadlines.detail: Vote at your assigned polling place. If you're in line by 7 p.m., you can vote.

deadlines.label: Mailed ballots must arrive
deadlines.detail: A mailed ballot must be postmarked on or before Election Day and received by your registrar by noon on the third day after the election.

students.q: Can I register at my college address?
students.a: Yes. Virginia says a dorm or college address can be your residential address for voting. You can only be registered in one place at a time, so pick school or home.

students.q: Is my student ID enough at the polls?
students.a: A valid student ID from a Virginia college, university or high school works. A student photo ID from any U.S. college or university also works.

students.q: Can I use my out-of-state driver's license?
students.a: No. Virginia's ID chart lists out-of-state driver's licenses as not accepted. Bring a student ID or another accepted ID instead.

students.q: What if I forget my ID?
students.a: You can sign an ID Confirmation Statement and vote a regular ballot. If you don't show ID or sign the statement, you'll vote a provisional ballot.

students.q: I'm registered at home but live at school. How do I vote?
students.a: Request a mail ballot by 5 p.m. on Oct. 23. You can mail it back (postmarked by Election Day), drop it at your voter registration office, a drop-off location or a satellite location before Election Day, or drop it at your voter registration office, any polling place or a drop-off location by 7 p.m. on Election Day.
